title: Operator Handshake and Initialization Contract: Service Bootstrap Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary

Purpose:
This page defines the operator-facing "initialization contract" and runtime handshake used when a service process comes online in Redwood Inference. It standardizes the signals, telemetry, and observability obligations that ensure a safe health handoff to upper-layer routing and autoscaling systems. The goal is to make cold start, warmup, and graceful scale events predictable and measurable across heterogeneous runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private).

Scope:
- Applies to all stateless and stateful services that participate in inference request routing (edge proxies, model workers, kv-coordinators, routing agents).
- Focuses on: startup sequence, readiness/healthy handoff, prewarm semantics, cache warming signals, and operator-level rollback/disable controls.
- Does NOT replace service-specific application health checks; it augments them with a standardized contract for platform tooling.

Ownership and contact:
- Owner team: engineering (Runtime and Infra SRE)
- Primary author: Maya Chen (Runtime Platform)
- Reviewers: Aaron Patel (SRE), Lucia Moretti (Runtime)
- Pager for bootstrap incidents: runtime-oncall@redwood.internal

Definitions and key signals:
- BOOTSTRAP_COMPLETE: service emits when initialization logic and mandatory attachments (KV, model artifact) are ready for traffic.
- PREFILLED_CACHE: optional tag indicating the service preloaded model KV/prefix caches sufficient for target QPS. Value: boolean.
- ACCEPTS_TRAFFIC: final signal used by the control plane to add the instance to router pools. Should only be true after SLO gating checks.
- DEGRADED_STARTUP: emitted when service can accept a reduced-fidelity workload (e.g., smaller batch sizes or quantized model) and should be considered for low-priority traffic.

Contract: signals, endpoints, and schema
1) Health and readiness endpoints (required):
   - /healthz (GET) — returns 200 + JSON {"status":"ok"} when process is alive.
   - /readiness (GET) — returns JSON with the required keys (see example). MUST be served on the same port as application and respond within 100ms under nominal load.

   Example readiness payload (JSON):
   {
     "status": "ready",
     "bootstrap_version": "2026-01-01-rc2",
     "components": {"model_artifact":"loaded","kv_coordinator":"connected"},
     "prefilled_cache": "partial",
     "observability_token": "sha1:...",
     "accepts_traffic": false
   }

2) Bootstrap event bus (recommended):
   - Emit structured bootstrap events to telemetry (prod.telemetry.bootstrap) with keys: event_type, instance_id, duration_ms, cause, prefill_level.
   - Minimum set: BOOTSTRAP_START, BOOTSTRAP_COMPLETE, PREFILL_PROGRESS, BOOTSTRAP_FAILED.

3) Liveness/Readiness semantics:
   - Liveness (/healthz) must reflect process crashability; do not return non-200 for temporary downstream failures.
   - Readiness must gate AcceptsTraffic; readiness=="ready" and accepts_traffic==true are required for routing.

Observability requirements (what to emit)
- Metrics (time-series):
  - bootstrap_duration_ms (histogram) with labels {service, model_variant, region, prefill_level}
  - prefilling_bytes_loaded (gauge)
  - accepts_traffic{yes/no} (gauge 0/1)
  - startup_error_count (counter) with error_code label

- Traces/events:
  - A single trace spanning BOOTSTRAP_START -> BOOTSTRAP_COMPLETE with spans for: config-load, model-open, kv-attach, cache-populate, readiness-declare. Maximum trace sampling rate: 5% by default; gateway may request debug sampling.

- Logs:
  - Structured JSON logs for bootstrap events with keys: ts, instance_id, event, details, duration_ms, level.

Startup gating and SLOs (examples and thresholds)
- Target median bootstrap_duration_ms <= 3500ms for dedicated GPU workers under nominal artifact sizes.
- 95th percentile <= 20s. If 95p exceeds 20s for three consecutive releases, block rollout.
- Prefill quality: PREFILLED_CACHE=="full" or "partial". If 'partial' is frequent and correlates with increased tail latency, schedule a prewarm capacity increase.

Prewarm vs coldstart behaviors
- Prewarm (recommended): platform will keep a configurable pool of prewarmed processes with prefilled caches. Prewarmed instances MUST report prefilling_bytes_loaded and PREFILLED_CACHE=="full" once warm.
- Coldstart: process must emit BOOTSTRAP_START on first acceptance of resources and write progress to telemetry. The platform will avoid routing full-fidelity traffic until ACCEPTS_TRAFFIC is true.

Graceful handoff and degradation modes
1) Progressive acceptance: When ACCEPTS_TRAFFIC flips to true, services should accept a ramped traffic profile (0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100%) controlled by platform for 2 minutes per step unless latency or error SLIs are violated.
2) DEGRADED_STARTUP: Services may advertise a DEGRADED_STARTUP capability with description of degraded behavior (e.g., "quantized: true, batch_size: 1"). Platform may route low-priority or experimental requests to these instances.

Operator controls and emergency flags
- /operator/disable (POST) — platform sends this to remove instance from routing and trigger a safe shutdown. Service must respond with 202 and begin drain.
- /operator/rollback (POST) — request service to discard current model artifact and reload previous version. This endpoint is rate-limited by control plane.
- Emergency TTL: any operator-disable event must be completed (instance removed from router and emptied of active requests) within 30s for edge proxies and 90s for model workers; longer drains must be explicitly negotiated and annotated in telemetry.

Kubernetes recommended integration (examples)
- Readiness probe config (deployment snippet):
  readinessProbe:
    httpGet:
      path: /readiness
      port: 8080
    initialDelaySeconds: 1
    periodSeconds: 3
    timeoutSeconds: 1
    failureThreshold: 3

- Liveness probe should point at /healthz but avoid depending on external KV connectivity.

Compatibility matrix and versioning
- The readiness schema is versioned in the readiness payload as "bootstrap_version" and a separate "readiness_schema_version". Platform accepts 1.x and 2.x formats; new schema changes require a migration ADR and 2-release deprecation timeline.

Rollout gating and acceptance tests (preflight)
1) Preflight checks before enabling ACCEPTS_TRAFFIC in production:
   - bootstrap_duration_ms median and 95p within acceptable limits on canary (see thresholds).
   - No bootstrap-related errors in last 500 instances.
   - Trace sampling confirms all bootstrap spans present for 98% of instances.

2) Automated tests:
   - Local unit test: readiness schema validation.
   - Integration: start service with mocked kv and model artifact and assert ACCEPTS_TRAFFIC transitions within 5s for dev-mode artifacts.

Runbook: what to do when an instance fails bootstrap
1) Detect: high bootstrap_duration_ms or repeated BOOTSTRAP_FAILED events.
2) Triage steps (operator):
   - Query telemetry: prod.telemetry.bootstrap for instance_id.
   - Inspect last readiness payload: curl -s http://{instance}/readiness | jq .
   - If error_code indicates artifact mismatch, trigger /operator/rollback.
   - If prefilling bytes stall, escalate to runtime-oncall and open a ticket with stack traces plus prefilling progress.
3) Temporary mitigation: mark new instances as DEGRADED_STARTUP and route only low priority traffic until fix.

Checklist for service owners (pre-deploy)
- Implement /healthz and /readiness per schema.
- Emit BOOTSTRAP_* events to telemetry.
- Provide operator endpoints (/operator/disable, /operator/rollback).
- Add bootstrap_duration_ms and prefilling_bytes_loaded metrics.
- Include readiness_schema_version and bootstrap_version in readiness payload.
- Add automated preflight suite to CI; ensure canary passes gating checks prior to full rollout.

ADR and migration guidance
- Any breaking change to readiness schema requires an ADR with: migration plan, compatibility shim for 2 releases, and synthetic test plan.
- For changes to operator endpoints (add/remove), use feature flags and staged rollout with explicit operator acceptance.

Appendix: example readiness JSON (full)
{
  "status": "ready",
  "bootstrap_version": "2026-01-01-rc2",
  "readiness_schema_version": "1.0",
  "components": {"model_artifact":"loaded","kv_coordinator":"connected","metrics_exporter":"ok"},
  "prefilled_cache": "partial",
  "prefilling_bytes_loaded": 21474836,
  "accepts_traffic": false,
  "capabilities": {"degraded_startup": true, "quantized_modes": ["int8"]},
  "notes": "warmup>prefill at 50%: will accept low-priority traffic after gating"
}

File a follow-up PR on this page or contact runtime-oncall@redwood.internal. Exceptions to timing thresholds must include compensating controls and SRE approval.
